# The central platform's wire error codes, and the client-local codes that share
# their namespace. Read by code_test.go, which asserts every Code* constant in
# this package appears below.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (2026-09-15, 人工拍板). Until today the registry was
# `the control-plane contract` §3.2, and code_test.go read that
# document at test time. The document was deleted because a design-first contract
# kept generating requirements the code had already outgrown; the interface
# contract is now regenerated FROM the code instead of ahead of it. The registry
# could not simply die with it: it is a SUPERSET of what this package implements
# (`safety_blocked`, `account_restricted`, … arrive with later work), and that
# superset exists nowhere in Go. So it moved here, next to the code that consumes
# it, where it is data rather than prose.
#
# It is a superset on purpose. The check in code_test.go is forward-only: a code
# this package knows must be registered here. "Registered here but not yet
# implemented" is an expected state, not drift.
#
# Format: `<http-status> <code>` for codes the platform returns, and
# `local <code>` for fail-closed codes this client produces itself. Blank lines
# and `#` comments are ignored. Order within a status group is not significant.

# 400 — the request was malformed or a form field was rejected.
400 invalid_phone
400 invalid_code
400 code_not_sent
400 activation_invalid
400 activation_code_used
400 box_code_unknown
400 box_code_mismatch
400 invalid_request

# 401 — the access token is missing, expired or rejected.
401 unauthorized
401 token_expired

# 402 — the account cannot pay for this request. The client must never predict
# this code locally: a free plan at zero balance may still be allowed to send
# (PQ8), so the entry point stays visible regardless of balance.
402 insufficient_credits

# 403 — the account is known but not allowed to do this. Kept distinct from 401:
# the remedy differs per code and none of them is "sign in again".
403 activation_required
403 plan_expired
403 feature_not_entitled
403 model_not_allowed
403 phone_mismatch
403 safety_blocked
403 content_restricted
403 account_restricted
403 box_access_denied

# 404
404 model_not_found
404 box_not_found

# 409 — a request with this id is already in flight; do not start a second model
# call, query its status instead.
409 request_in_progress
409 duplicate_request
409 idempotency_conflict

# 429 — cool down for retryAfterSec; never retry concurrently.
429 rate_limited

# 503
503 maintenance
503 box_unavailable

# 5xx — retry with bounded backoff, and for a repeated clientRequestId query the
# request status before deciding whether to resend.
5xx upstream_unavailable
5xx internal_error

# Codes this client produces itself. They are not platform responses, yet they
# share the namespace because the frontend maps them in the same table — a
# locally-produced refusal without a code would force the UI to match on prose,
# which fails silently the first time the wording changes (V-55).
local catalog_signature_invalid
local policy_expired
local bootstrap_stale
local usage_pending
local network_unavailable
local model_withdrawn
local catalog_unavailable
local model_unavailable
local input_sensitive

# Envelope field names. Fixed: these six, and no second naming scheme
# (`messageKey`, `traceId`). `message` is for humans and must not be rendered;
# `requestId` is what correlates a client log with a platform ticket.
# `phoneMasked` accompanies phone_mismatch only, and carries the masked phone the
# activation code is already bound to — the client cannot know it, and the UI has
# to be able to say which number the directory is bound to.
field code
field message
field field
field retryAfterSec
field requestId
field phoneMasked
